creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The most-cited item across both review sources. Interpolating untrusted text into `$` executes it:

```rad
payload = `a"; echo INJECTED; echo "b`
$`echo "{payload}"`
// a
// INJECTED
// b
```

Bare interpolation word-splits too: ``$`echo {spaced}` `` with `spaced = "one two"` arrives as two arguments. `executeShellCmd` (`core/shell.go:116`) hands the interpolated string to `exec.Command` verbatim.

Four data points in #153 (needles, filenames, HN and Reddit thread titles, LLM prose), and five separate hand-rolled quoters in the script corpus: `cct:124-125`, `devenv:246-248`, `laptop:61-63`, `fr:37-38`, `peer:102-104`. `star:96-101` pipes Kafka payloads through `echo '{payload}' | jq` and breaks today on any payload containing a single quote. The kan hooks in this repo interpolate third-party Jira issue summaries and user-typed card titles straight into commands.

`shellQuote` already exists at `core/completion.go:141` - the POSIX single-quote idiom, tested on the hard case at `core/interactive_args_test.go:427` (`it's` becomes `'it'\''s'`). It is unexported and used only for completion and interactive-arg rendering. For POSIX shells this looks close to an export.

`shell_cmds.md` (2024-10) judged injection safety not a major concern for the use case. The agent-facing hooks that feed third-party text into commands did not exist then; that is the counter-evidence.

Two things this card does not settle: the pwsh and cmd.exe fallback, which is the real work, and whether an argv-form `$[...]` should exist alongside the quoting primitive. That second question has its own card in stretch. The primitive is useful either way.

`rad docs guide/shell-commands` currently teaches ``$`git commit -m "{message}"` ``, whose hand-placed quotes break on the first `"` in `message`. That example is probably what should teach whatever lands.

---

### Orientation

- `core/` owns shell execution. `core/shell.go:116` `executeShellCmd` evaluates the interpolated command down to one string and hands it to `RShell`, the injectable executor seam. `core/shell.go:171` `realShellExecutor` is the production implementation; it builds `<shell> <flag> <string>` at `core/shell.go:315` `buildCmd`. The card's `core/shell.go:116` pointer is correct.
- The new function is an ordinary public builtin: docs-first in `docs/funcs/`, then registered in `core/funcs.go`. `rts/` learns the signature through codegen and must not be hand-edited.
- The docs fix lands in `docs-web/docs/guide/shell-commands.md`. `core/embedded_docs/` is the generated mirror.

### Where to start

- `core/completion.go:141` `shellQuote` is the POSIX single-quote idiom that already exists (`'` plus the `'\''` escape). `core/interactive_args.go:981` `shellQuoteIfNeeded` wraps it with a shell-inert-token bypass. `core/interactive_args_test.go:427` asserts `it's` becomes `'it'\''s'`. Both card pointers check out.
- Adding the builtin, in order: write `docs/funcs/shell_escape.md` to the contract in `docs/funcs/README.md` (required sections in order; the `## Signature` line IS the type-checker's signature, there is no parallel Go definition), run `make generate`, then add the `FUNC_SHELL_ESCAPE` const to the block at `core/funcs.go:38-64` and register the `BuiltInFunc`. `core/funcs.go:536` (`FUNC_UPPER`) is the smallest inline example; `core/func_split.go` is the separate-file form.
- The platform question is `core/shell.go:264` `resolveShell`: Windows tries `pwsh.exe`, then `powershell.exe`, then `cmd.exe`; everything else gets `/bin/sh`. `core/shell.go:304` `shellExecFlag` is where `cmd.exe`'s `/c` is distinguished from `-c`. A quoting function that assumes POSIX is wrong on two of those three.
- Docs example to replace: `docs-web/docs/guide/shell-commands.md:175` carries the ``$`git commit -m "{message}"` `` form. `docs-web/docs/guide/defer-errdefer.md:109` has the same shape.
- Prior reasoning the card cites is at `docs/thinking/shell_cmds.md`.

### How to verify

- `make build`, then `./bin/radd script.rad` on a script interpolating ``a"; echo INJECTED; echo "b``.
- Function snapshots go under `core/testing/snapshots/functions/`. Update with `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=functions` (the `=` is required; a bare `-update` swallows `-run`).
- Doc snippets in `docs-web/docs/` are validated by `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go:102` `TestDocSnippets`, which runs them through `rts/check`. A rewritten guide example that does not check clean fails the suite: `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestDocSnippets`.
- `make generate && make verify-generated`, then `make all`.

### Done when

- `docs/funcs/shell_escape.md` exists and `make generate` leaves no diff afterward.
- The builtin is registered and snapshot-tested, including embedded single quotes, embedded double quotes, and the empty string.
- The platform story is decided and stated in the function doc: either the function is POSIX-only and says so plainly, or it dispatches on what `resolveShell` picked.
- `docs-web/docs/guide/shell-commands.md` no longer teaches the hand-quoted form, and the replacement snippet passes `TestDocSnippets`.

### Watch out for

- Do not call `os/exec` or read `SHELL` directly from the builtin. Everything goes through the seams in `core/global.go` (`RShell` and friends) - that is what lets `core/testing/` run the real runner against fakes.
- If quoting has to vary by shell, the platform branch belongs in `core/common/platform.go` per the repo convention, not as a scattered `runtime.GOOS` check.
- Generated and never hand-edited: `core/embedded_docs/`, `docs-web/docs/reference/functions.md`, `rts/signatures_gen.go`, `rts/embedded_funcs/`, `rts/embedded/functions.txt`.
- A `shell_escape()` that emits POSIX quoting on Windows is worse than no function at all: it reads as safe and is not. If the pwsh and cmd.exe paths are out of scope, that limitation belongs in the function doc, not just the commit message.
title: Add shell_escape(), and fix the docs example teaching the broken idiom
